components.name: Load Balancer
components.summary: Spreads requests over every app server behind it, and stops sending to one that fails its health check.
components.tradeoff: Cheap and takes 100k requests a second, but one load balancer is a single point of failure: run two.

components.name: App Server
components.examples: a Spring Boot, Node.js or Go service on VMs or containers
components.summary: Runs your code: takes requests, reads and writes stores, answers. About 2 000 requests a second each.
components.tradeoff: Stateless, so you scale it out by adding replicas. One instance fails about 0.5% of the time.

components.name: SQL Database
components.summary: Strongly consistent rows with transactions. Each replica serves about 20 000 reads a second; every write goes to one primary (5 000 a second).
components.tradeoff: Read replicas add reads, not writes: for more writes, shard. A replica to promote turns a long outage into a short failover.

components.name: Cache
components.summary: Keeps hot data in memory: 100 000 reads a second at about 1 ms. Wire it to an app server and its reads go cache-aside.
components.tradeoff: Only as good as its hit ratio. When it restarts cold or a hot key expires, every miss lands on the database at once.

components.name: CDN
components.summary: Answers cacheable requests from a data center near the user, before they reach you. Far users stop paying the ocean crossing.
components.tradeoff: Only helps with responses that can be cached and shared; it does nothing for writes or per-user data.

components.name: Queue
components.summary: Takes a message durably in a few milliseconds, so the request can answer now and a worker does the slow part later.
components.tradeoff: Work becomes eventual: if workers fall behind, the backlog grows and users wait minutes for the result.

components.name: Worker
components.examples: a consumer service, AWS Lambda on SQS, Celery, Sidekiq
components.summary: Takes jobs from a queue and does them: writes, emails, fan-out. About 2 000 jobs a second each.
components.tradeoff: Scale it on the backlog, not on CPU: a worker that keeps up at the average falls behind at the peak.

components.name: Firewall (WAF)
components.summary: Stops bots, scrapers and attacks at the edge, before they cost you an app server or a database read.
components.tradeoff: Another hop and another bill; it blocks known-bad traffic, not a flood of real users.

components.name: Object Storage
components.examples: Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, Cloudflare R2
components.summary: Holds files and blobs of any size, cheaply and durably. Scales without you managing instances.
components.tradeoff: Slow per request (tens of ms), and every byte sent to the internet is billed as egress: put a CDN in front of downloads.

components.name: API Gateway
components.summary: Authenticates, rate-limits and routes API calls. Rejects bot floods with 429 before they reach an app server.
components.tradeoff: About 10 000 requests a second each, and 10 ms more on every call.

components.name: NoSQL Database
components.summary: Partitioned by key: every replica takes 20 000 reads and 20 000 writes a second, so writes scale out.
components.tradeoff: Eventually consistent by default: a read may miss the latest write. Never use it where two users must not get the same seat.

components.name: Search Index
components.summary: An inverted index for full-text and filtered queries the database cannot do fast.
components.tradeoff: About 3 000 queries a second each, and it lags the database: feed it asynchronously.

components.name: Data Warehouse
components.summary: Columnar storage for analytics over billions of rows.
components.tradeoff: Built for big scans, not for traffic: about 200 requests a second. Load it in batches from a queue.

features.name: Instance sizes
features.summary: Pick M (2× capacity for 1.8× the price) or L (4× for 3.5×) for app servers, workers, caches and databases. L is the biggest box there is: after that, scale out.

features.name: Sharding
features.summary: Split a database into partitions, each with its own primary: write capacity grows with every shard.

features.name: Wide lanes
features.summary: Six components per lane instead of four.
